
[[File:Rdr combat.jpg|border|300px|right]]

'''Combat''' is a major element of gameplay in the ''[[Red Dead]]'' series, namely ''[[Red Dead Revolver]]'', ''[[Red Dead Redemption]]'', ''[[Red Dead Redemption 2]]'' and ''[[Red Dead Online]]''.

==Description==
Combat is required as part of many story missions in all games as well as in side missions and [[Random Encounters]] in ''Red Dead Redemption'' and ''Red Dead Redemption 2''. In [[Redemption Multiplayer|multiplayer]] it is the primary focus of gameplay.

There are many forms of combat. While gunplay is a central component of each game, combat can also be performed with melee attacks, [[Thrown Weapons]], and mounted weapons. The player can fight on foot, behind cover, on horseback, or from moving vehicles such as [[Trains]] and [[Stagecoaches]].

==Cover==
Taking cover is a very important part of combat. The player is exposed on horseback and on foot, while walls and other objects can provide protection. [[Arthur Morgan]], [[John Marston]] or [[Jack Marston]] can 'hug' walls, crates, or rocks and can hide in bushes; he can open (or close) doors while in cover; they can lean out and shoot or, in ''Redemption,'' fire blindly at enemies. While in cover, press the button again while holding the stick towards a second piece of cover (e.g. opposite side of a door, nearby crate/rock) and the player will dash into the new cover. The cover system has changed a little from another Rockstar series, ''Grand Theft Auto''. In the ''GTA'' series, the player still had a crosshair while blind-firing. Now Marston, as well as the player, has no clue what he'll hit. It's not an effective way of fighting, but it can give the player some breathing time and suppress the enemies for a while.
:'''Note''': Taking cover in ''[[Undead Nightmare]]'' is not recommended as the undead will pursue you wherever you may be. Using melee, they will go around whatever you are hiding behind, making cover a futile system in the DLC pack. If you attack a survivor in Undead Nightmare, then they will attack you as if they would in the original game. This situation makes cover a valuable system, although dead eye could simply be used as it is rare to fight more than one human at a time.

==Fistfight/Knife fight==
In all three installments, you can also engage in a close- range brawl, called a "fistfight". On many special occasions some enemies may get into brawls with the player at close-range. If a fistfight occurs in ''Redemption 2,'' there are two types of buttons the player needs to remember: the "Block" button ({{PSSQ}} (PS4) or {{XBX}} (ONE)) or (R (PC)) and the "Attack" button ({{PSCIR}} (PS4) or {{XBB}} (ONE)) or (F (PC)).

The trick to winning the brawl is to always be on the defensive. The player (Arthur or John) will want to start blocking against attacks using the "Block" button, and the moment that they block an attack, they will want to immediately press the "Attack" button to retaliate with an attack of their own. The player can chain two or three quick punches immediately after they've blocked an attack, but the longer they continue punching, the more likely their opponent is to block them and start laying into the player with punches of their own.

Melee weapons like a knife or hatchet can also be useful when the going gets tough, especially if an opponent carries a knife with them for a knife fight.

==Other==
Arthur or John has a variety of other skills, like [[Dead-Eye Targeting]] or rolling. He can roll in any direction he chooses, which is a great opportunity to evade an incoming bullet/stagecoach/angry bull and such. Arthur or John can replenish Dead Eye and health during battle, using [[Chewing Tobacco]], [[Moonshine]], [[Snake Oil]] and [[Tonic]].

==Euphoria==
[[Euphoria]] is a character behavior system from NaturalMotion, used by [[Rockstar Games]], in conjunction with the RAGE engine, in many games, like ''Red Dead Redemption'' or ''GTA IV''. It simulates human behavior. For example, when the player shoots a humanoid enemy in a leg, he'll still walk, but with a noticeable limp on the injured leg. If the player shoots the enemy in both his legs, he will lie on his knees and shoot the player, and then perish shortly after. If an enemy is shot at the end of the spinal cord (the lower back), it will put the enemy into a crawling state, leaving them to moan and sputter death-related comments, then die a few moments later. Another example has the player killing an enemy when they are firing at you with a pistol/revolver. When the player fires the fatal shot, as the enemy falls to the ground, they will fire one last shot, as a last ditch effort.
